definitions.definition: For every integer r≥0, Y_r=y^r/r!, including Y_0=Id_V.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra acting on V
definitions.definition: U_Z is the integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(C) generated by X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! for all integers r≥0; its action on V is the given representation extended to the enveloping algebra.

definitions.type: subring of Q, embedded in C
definitions.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b∈Q:a,b∈Z and p does not divide b}, with operations inherited from Q. A unit of R means an element having a multiplicative inverse in R.
M_R is the R-span of M in V, namely all finite sums of r_j m_j with r_j∈R and m_j∈M. The canonical map R⊗_Z M→M_R sends r⊗m to rm; its injectivity is to be proved, not assumed.
For i,j∈I, E_ij is the unique complex-linear map with E_ij(e_k)=δ_jk e_i for all k∈I, where δ_jk is 1 if j=k and 0 otherwise. This construction requires that e be a complex basis of V.

definitions.type: family of R-submodules of C indexed by I
definitions.definition: For each i∈I, J_i={c∈C:c e_i∈M_R}, with addition and R-action inherited from C.

V(K)=M⊗_Z K. Here tensor products have their usual balanced-module meaning: they are generated by pure tensors subject to additivity in each argument and (am)⊗c=m⊗(ac) for the base scalar a. Induced lattice endomorphisms act on the M factor; the same symbols x,y,h denote these induced K-linear operators once preservation of M is established.

inputs.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and 0≤λ<p.
V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ and complex dimension λ+1. The Chevalley generator endomorphisms satisfy hx-xh=2x, hy-yh=-2y, and xy-yx=h.

M is an admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup of V admitting an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and is stable under U_Z. The choice of M is arbitrary, not restricted to the minimal lattice.

e=(e_i)_{i∈I} is a complex basis of V. For every integer t≥0, hy^t v=(λ-2t)y^t v; for t≥1, xy^t v=t(λ-t+1)y^{t-1}v. Also y^{λ+1}v=0 and all higher powers on v vanish. On the basis, xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ-i+1)e_{i-1} for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ-2i)e_i. For all natural r and i∈I, X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_{i-r} if r≤i, and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤λ, and zero otherwise. All displayed divided-power coefficients are integers.

The map R⊗_Z M→M_R, a_R⊗m↦a_R m, is an R-linear isomorphism, M_R has an R-basis indexed by I, and its complex span is V. Each X_r and Y_r for r≥0 preserves M_R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1} X_{λ-i}(Y_λ X_λ)Y_{λ-j}. In particular every E_ij preserves M_R. More explicitly Y_λX_λ=E_{λλ}, X_{λ-i}E_{λλ}=E_{iλ}, and E_{λλ}Y_{λ-j}=binom(λ,j)E_{λj}.

For all i∈I, J_i=J; J is nonzero and finitely generated over R; M_R=⊕_{i∈I} J e_i inside V. The multiplication map Q⊗_R J→C, q⊗c↦qc, is injective and dim_Q(Q⊗_R J)=1. There exists b∈J with b≠0 and J=Rb, and for every such b, (b e_i)_{i∈I} is an R-basis of M_R.

Let A be a commutative semiring, B a semiring with an A-algebra structure, T an additive commutative monoid and A-module, and C an index type. For an A-basis d:C→T and c∈C, the canonical scalar-extension basis d.baseChange(B), a B-basis of B⊗_A T indexed by C, satisfies d.baseChange(B)(c)=1⊗d(c).

inputs.statement: For natural numbers d and q, if q is prime, then q divides d! if and only if q≤d.
source_conditions: d and q are natural numbers and q is prime.

output.statement: The integer map Z→K extends to a ring map R→K by a/d↦(a in K)/(d in K). There are natural K-linear isomorphisms M⊗_Z K≃M_R⊗_R K≃(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K, where F_p=Z/pZ and its map to K is induced by the integer map. There exists a K-basis β=(β_i)_{i∈I} of V(K), arising as the scalar extensions of b e_i for a nonzero b∈J with J=Rb, on which xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ-i+1)β_{i-1} for i≥1, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, hβ_i=(λ-2i)β_i, with integer coefficients read in K. For every such basis define ε_ij by ε_ij β_k=δ_jk β_i. All binom(λ,j) and all r! for 0≤r≤λ are nonzero in K; induced divided powers satisfy X_r=(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r=(r!)^{-1}y^r in that range, and ε_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1} X_{λ-i}(Y_λX_λ)Y_{λ-j}. Thus every K-subspace invariant under x,y is invariant under every ε_ij.

binders.type: integer with p not dividing d
family of K-linear endomorphisms indexed by I×I

locals.declaration: Choose b≠0 in J with J=Rb, using N003.
Define ρ(a/d)=(a in K)/(d in K) for p not dividing d; well-definedness is established in S001.
Define F_p=Z/pZ with its natural map to K.
Define β_i to be the image of (b e_i)⊗1 under the inverse of the first isomorphism constructed in S002.
After establishing in S003 that β is a basis, define ε_ij by ε_ij β_k=δ_jk β_i.

argument.text: Choose b as in N003. Since K has characteristic p by H001, the kernel of Z→K is pZ: Euclidean division by p reduces any integer to a remainder 0≤s<p, and the definition of characteristic says no positive such remainder maps to zero. Consequently any integer d not divisible by p has nonzero image in K. Define ρ(a/d)=a_K/d_K on R. Equality of fractions is cross-multiplication in Z, hence in K; their denominators remain nonzero, proving well-definedness, additivity and multiplicativity. Thus ρ extends the integer map. Its kernel is pR, since a/d maps to zero exactly when p divides a. Reduction sends a/d modulo p to a times the inverse of d in F_p=Z/pZ, giving R/pR≃F_p with the natural inclusion F_p→K. The latter is injective by the same characteristic argument. Also X_1=x and Y_1=y preserve M by H004; H002 gives h=xy-yx, so h preserves M too. All induced lattice actions in D012 are therefore defined.

produces.statement: ρ:R→K is a well-defined ring map extending Z→K with kernel pR, and R/pR≃F_p=Z/pZ compatibly with the natural injection F_p→K. The operators x,y,h preserve M.

argument.text: Use N002 to identify M_R with R⊗_Z M. The first isomorphism sends m⊗c in M⊗_Z K to m⊗c in M_R⊗_R K, equivalently (1⊗m)⊗c. Its inverse sends (r⊗m)⊗c to m⊗ρ(r)c. Integer and R-balancing verify both maps, and their composites fix every pure tensor, hence all finite sums. For the second isomorphism send u⊗c to (u+pM_R)⊗c. The inverse sends (u+pM_R)⊗c to u⊗c; changing u by pz changes the result by z⊗pc=0. Balancing over F_p follows from F000 and the R-action through R/pR; the same pure tensor check shows inverse composites. These maps are K-linear and intertwine every induced R-linear lattice operator, as is checked on pure tensors.

produces.statement: There are K-linear isomorphisms V(K)=M⊗_Z K≃M_R⊗_R K≃(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K with exactly the maps displayed in S002; they intertwine all induced lattice operators.

argument.text: N003 says (b e_i) is an R-basis of M_R. Applying M001 with R→K makes the vectors 1⊗(b e_i) a K-basis of K⊗_R M_R. The flip of pure tensors, c⊗u↔u⊗c, is balanced and has itself as inverse, so it identifies this basis with (b e_i)⊗1 in M_R⊗_R K. Transporting through F001 defines β_i and proves β is a K-basis of V(K). Reduction of the R-basis modulo p is also a basis over F_p: its coordinates identify M_R with R^I and pM_R with (pR)^I, hence the quotient with (R/pR)^I. The second isomorphism in F001 therefore gives the same basis by reduction and extension. N001 applied to b e_i (b is a complex scalar) gives exactly xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ-i+1)β_{i-1}, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, hβ_i=(λ-2i)β_i, with the boundary restrictions on x as in N001 and all coefficients mapped to K. Define ε_ij to be the matrix units for this basis. By N002, E_ij preserve M_R and hence induce these ε_ij, and their product identities persist by F001.

produces.statement: β is a K-basis of V(K) obtained from b e_i by the scalar-extension maps. Its operator formulas are xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ-i+1)β_{i-1} for i≥1, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, hβ_i=(λ-2i)β_i, for i∈I. Induced E_ij are ε_ij, and ε_ij=ρ(binom(λ,j))^{-1} X_{λ-i}(Y_λX_λ)Y_{λ-j}, where X,Y here denote induced divided-power operators.

argument.text: For each 0≤r≤λ<p, M007 gives p not dividing r!, so its image in K is nonzero by F000. On the original lattice r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r, and both sides preserve M. Thus after scalar extension X_r=(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r=(r!)^{-1}y^r in this range. N002 states binom(λ,j) is a unit in R; its image in K is a unit since ρ sends its inverse to an inverse. F002 therefore gives ε_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1}X_{λ-i}(Y_λX_λ)Y_{λ-j}. A subspace invariant under x,y is invariant under their nonnegative powers, scalar multiples and compositions, so this formula proves its invariance under every ε_ij. All indices used here lie between 0 and λ. The argument works for any witness b allowed by N003, establishing the stated universal assertions.
